facts.advisory_summary: Authorization bypass in github.com/dgrijalva/jwt-go — jwt-go allows attackers to bypass intended access restrictions in situations with `[]string{}` for `m["aud"]` (which is allowed by the specification). Because the type assertion fails, "" is the value of aud. This is a security problem if the JWT token is presented to a service that lacks its own audience check. There is no patch available and users of jwt-go are advised to migrate to [golang-jwt](https://github.com/golang-jwt/jwt) at version 3.2.1

expect.note: The app authenticates with ozzo-routing auth.JWT (internal/auth/middleware.go:15), which uses jwt.Parser.Parse with MapClaims (ozzo-routing/v2@v2.3.0 auth/handlers.go:268-278); MapClaims.Valid in jwt-go v3.2.0 only checks exp/iat/nbf and never calls VerifyAudience. Neither the app nor ozzo-routing calls MapClaims.VerifyAudience anywhere, and the app does no audience check.
expect.labelled_by: claude-opus code read 2026-10-18 (blind: before any judge run; agent-labelled)

facts.advisory_summary: Excessive Platform Resource Consumption within a Loop in Kubernetes — The Kubernetes API Server component in versions 1.1-1.14, and versions prior to 1.15.10, 1.16.7 and 1.17.3 allows an authorized user who sends malicious YAML payloads to cause the kube-apiserver to consume excessive CPU cycles while parsing YAML.

expect.note: yaml.Unmarshal is called only in config.Load (internal/config/config.go:49) on the server's own config file, path from the -config CLI flag (cmd/server/main.go:29,37); no request data is ever parsed as YAML, and yaml.v2 is not used by other non-test deps (zap/ozzo only reference it in go.sum). Only an operator controlling the config file could trigger this.
expect.labelled_by: claude-opus code read 2026-10-18 (blind: before any judge run; agent-labelled)

facts.advisory_summary: YAML Go package vulnerable to denial of service — Due to unbounded alias chasing, a maliciously crafted YAML file can cause the system to consume significant system resources. If parsing user input, this may be used as a denial of service vector.

expect.note: yaml.Unmarshal is called only in config.Load (internal/config/config.go:49) on the local config file named by the -config flag (cmd/server/main.go:29,37); attacker-controlled data never reaches the YAML decoder, so unbounded alias chasing cannot be triggered remotely.
expect.labelled_by: claude-opus code read 2026-10-18 (blind: before any judge run; agent-labelled)
